heading: Asian Games 2026: Elavenil stars as shooters clinch two silver medals
author: Uthra Ganesan
paragraphs: Until the midway stage, Elavenil Valarivan was comfortably positioned at the top, with a lead that would, on any other day, be enough to keep her there until the end. On Sunday (September 20, 2026), Elavenil, the senior-most of the three Indian women in the 10m air rifle event, allowed her mind to get the better of her trigger finger, settling for a silver medal on the opening day of the Asian Games shooting competition.

Elavenil managed a total of 252.4 points over 24 shots, finishing 0.6 points behind Hinata Tanichi, the Japanese shooter who crawled her way to the top, one shot at a time. Korea’s reigning Olympic champion, Ban Hyojin, finished third. Once the top three were decided, it was all about the color of the medal.

Elavenil and India, though, had already assured themselves of a team silver even before the final began. Sonam Maskar and Vidarsa K. Vinod shooting high enough in the qualifying round ensured the three together would not go back empty-handed. Vidarsa shot 630.4, and with Sonam also qualifying for the top eight with an impressive 634.1, there were hopes of two Indians on the podium. And, for a while, the hopes seemed justified.

Sonam, in particular, had been very consistent throughout the qualifying rounds, not scoring below 105 in any of the six series of 10 shots each. However, one bad score on the 15th shot—a 9.9, her only poor shot of the day—ended her journey in sixth place. Elavenil, on the other hand, was in a different zone. Even as big names fell by the wayside—holder Han Jiayu was eliminated in seventh place, and reigning Olympic champion and World No. 1 Wang Zefei finished fifth—the 27-year-old kept increasing her lead.

Once the medallists were decided, however, it looked like Elavenil abruptly took her foot off the gas. Her scores dropped from the high 10s to the low 10s; she had a couple of 10.1s, and it was clear the spell had broken. Her lead at the top was still good enough to make it to the last two shots but its gradual erosion also saw the top spot and the gold slipping away.

Earlier, Vidarsa, having started strongly in the qualifications, ended with two low rounds of 104. 3 and 104.4, the last two series pulling her down to 12th place. Qualifications World Record holder Wang, meanwhile, added a new Games and Asian qualifying record to her kitty with a total of 636.8.
